key_provisions: Would have expanded I-Bank financing eligibility for projects capturing and converting data center waste heat.

status: Approved by Governor and chaptered 2026-09-21, Chapter 434, Statutes of 2026; ordinary effective date 2027-01-01.
key_provisions: Requires CEC facility reporting upon energization or substantive changes and at least annual energy reporting, generally disaggregated monthly, for data centers of at least 10 MW; local discretionary permit applications must include energy and sound estimates. Includes specified facility exclusions and disclosure protections.

status: Official history observed 2026-11-06 New York time lists the 2025-08-29 Senate Appropriations hold under submission, after Assembly passage 2025-06-02 (57-18). The status page labels the measure Active Bill - In Committee Process; ultimate legal disposition remains unverified.
key_provisions: Would require data center power usage effectiveness reporting and cost-shift assessment in energy planning.

status: Approved by Governor and chaptered 2026-09-21, Chapter 435, Statutes of 2026; ordinary effective date 2027-01-01.
key_provisions: CPUC must require electrical corporations to file data center transmission, distribution and generation tariffs; generation tariffs include cost-recovery mechanisms of at least 10 years. Community choice aggregators and electric service providers must adopt generation tariffs by 2028-01-01.

status: Approved by Governor and chaptered 2026-09-21, Chapter 436, Statutes of 2026; ordinary effective date 2027-01-01.
key_provisions: Conditions local discretionary or ministerial permits for data center construction or expansion increasing maximum peak water use on a water supply assessment, projected water use and efficiency measures, workforce disclosures, and applicant payment of required water infrastructure costs. A water scarcity plan is additionally required beginning 2028-01-01; satisfying these conditions does not compel approval.

status: Approved by Governor and chaptered 2026-09-21, Chapter 437, Statutes of 2026; ordinary effective date 2027-01-01.
key_provisions: Requires data center water-use estimates to water suppliers and local governments for initial licenses or permits and annual use reporting on renewals; includes data center demand in urban water suppliers’ shortage assessments.

status: Vetoed by Governor 2025-10-11; consideration of veto stricken from file 2026-01-22
key_provisions: Would have required data center water-use estimates and annual water-use reporting tied to business licenses and permits.

status: Approved by Governor and chaptered 2026-09-21, Chapter 440, Statutes of 2026; ordinary effective date 2027-01-01.
key_provisions: Directs CPUC to assess opportunities for rate structures addressing data center transmission and distribution costs, load and procurement costs, and residential cost pressures.

status: Failed; from committee and from Assembly without further action, 2024-11-30 (prior 2023-2024 session concluded)
key_provisions: Proposed certification/exemption framework for certain thermal powerplants linked to data centers, including backup generation and air district review.

status: Chaptered by Secretary of State, Ch. 647, Statutes of 2025, 2025-10-11
key_provisions: Authorizes CPUC to assess whether new data center loads shift electrical corporation costs to other customers; requires submission and public posting of an assessment completed under the section by 2027-01-01. Section 913.22 is repealed 2031-01-01.
end_condition: As enacted in Chapter 647, Statutes of 2025, Public Utilities Code section 913.22 is repealed on 2031-01-01.

status: Chaptered by Secretary of State, Ch. 438, Statutes of 2026, 2026-09-21; ordinary effective date 2027-01-01.
key_provisions: Requires CPUC by 2028-01-01 to establish or update tariffs and electric rules for participating customers, including protections against cost shifts and a transmission-level interconnection tariff with cost responsibility and early termination terms. Section 945.3 applies to data centers entering new transmission-level retail service interconnection agreements on or after 2027-01-01; demand response participation is optional.

status: Chaptered by Secretary of State, Ch. 439, Statutes of 2026, 2026-09-21; ordinary effective date 2027-01-01.
key_provisions: Removes categorical CEQA exemptions for data center development and operation, with specified facility exclusions; adds qualifying data center and geothermal powerplant projects to environmental leadership development project eligibility, subject to statutory conditions. This combines environmental review requirements with conditional judicial streamlining.

status: Official history observed 2026-11-06 New York time lists the 2026-05-14 hearing held in Senate Appropriations committee and under submission. This is the latest displayed action, not proof of no later unrecorded action or a terminal disposition.
key_provisions: March 23 amended proposal would establish a special rate structure for data centers taking transmission-level service with estimated peak demand of at least 75 MW, prevent cost shifts, require upfront infrastructure costs, enable prefunding of a 15-year incremental zero-carbon resources contract, and impose prevailing-wage and skilled-and-trained-workforce provisions. The earlier onsite solar/wind/battery-only backup clause is deleted in this version.

key_provisions: Requires annual energy and water consumption reporting by data centers and imposes penalties.

status: Passed House 197-5 on 2026-06-25; referred to Senate Finance Committee 2026-06-26; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: House-amended PN 3694 proposes repealing the Computer Data Center Equipment Incentive Program and denying specified other tax benefits to computer data centers unless certified under Article XXIX-D before 2026-02-03.

status: Passed House 116-84 on 2026-04-27; referred to Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee 2026-05-01; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Amends Title 27 water resources provisions for covered data centers; requires water-use review/reporting for facilities with proposed consumptive use above 100,000 gallons per day over 30 days.

status: Passed House 171-31 on 2026-06-30; referred to Senate Finance Committee 2026-07-10; no further Senate action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: House-amended PN 3724 proposes computer-data-center incentive certification and retention conditions: a community-protection plan, project-footprint reporting and specified NDA certification. The plan and NDA conditions exclude centers below 10 MW peak demand. Separate exceptions concern specified pre-construction engagement requirements where construction began earlier, and NDA certification for previously certified owners/operators or qualified tenants. This is not a general amendment banning every data-center NDA under the Right-to-Know Law.

status: Referred to House Energy Committee 2026-04-09; no further action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Pennsylvania Ratepayer Protection Act; requires hyperscale data centers to pay their own energy and interconnection infrastructure costs.

sponsors: Rep. Paul Friel (D), with 42 bipartisan co-sponsors
status: Passed House 201-1 on 2026-06-24; referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-25; reported as amended and re-referred to Senate Rules and Executive Nominations 2026-06-30.
key_provisions: Senate-amended PN 3727 would let a municipality adopt a public-meeting resolution pausing acceptance of new data-center land-development applications for up to 180 days, retroactive to specified public notice. Earlier applications are exempt and continue under the applicable earlier rules; submissions during a pause are deemed received the following day after it ends. Repeat use is barred for 18 months following formal expiration or repeal. This is optional local authority, not a statewide pause.
end_condition: If enacted and a municipality adopts a pause, it may last no more than 180 days, retroactive to the specified public notice; the same procedure may not be used again for 18 months after formal expiration or repeal.

sponsors: Rep. Paul Friel; Rep. Kyle Donahue; Rep. Kyle Mullins; Rep. Chris Pielli

status: Referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-04; reported as committed 10-1 on 2026-06-30; re-reported as amended (PN 1889) by Senate Rules and Executive Nominations 2026-07-11; second consideration in the Senate 2026-07-12. key_provisions: Re-reported PN 1889 proposes optional municipal resolutions temporarily pausing acceptance and consideration of specified new high-impact-data-center applications for up to 18 months, retroactive to the required public notice. It requires planning findings and hearing notice, preserves listed unrelated/maintenance activities, and exempts previously approved matters and qualifying pre-existing power-generation-site agreements. It does not itself enact a statewide or local moratorium.
end_condition: If enacted and locally invoked, PN 1889 would permit a temporary moratorium lasting no more than 18 months, retroactive to the required public-notice date.

key_provisions: Re-reported PN 2007 proposes a Data Center Transparency Act covering defined predominantly server-use facilities with peak electric demand of at least 10 MW. It combines specified public-agency NDA limits, at least two local public meetings and utility-application documentation before approval, restrictions on defined foreign-entity-controlled facilities, and energy/water-report certifications. Its proposed chapters have separate 180-day, immediate and 60-day commencement clauses; none supplies an enacted date here.

Defines data center at 1 MW or more.
